measurement.method: Host phases use perf_counter spans. Device phases use CUDA events on the inference stream. The profiler explicitly synchronizes at the existing result-extraction boundary, then separates device-to-host copies from Python conversion and result construction.
caveats: CUDA event and host wall durations overlap and must not be added together.
Event recording and phase clocks add diagnostic overhead, so the profiled wall time is not an optimized-throughput result.
Aggregate queue wait sums simultaneous per-request waits and is not an end-to-end wall-time component.
nvidia-smi utilization is retained as corroborating coarse telemetry, not used alone to identify the bottleneck.

batching_and_contention.interpretation: The queue formed 97.9%-full batches and spent little exclusive sampled wall time in batcher code. The 1.30 ms mean request wait is mostly useful coalescing inside the 2 ms bound, not evidence that lock contention dominates.

ranked_evidence_for_next_change.evidence: 40.892 s, or 65.30% of profiled inference wall time and 2.098 ms per batch; CPU encoding alone is 6.34x the CUDA-event model execution total.
ranked_evidence_for_next_change.next_experiment: Reduce repeated Python/tensor construction in canonical CPU encoding while keeping encoding version 1 byte-for-byte equivalent.

ranked_evidence_for_next_change.evidence: 4.942 s, or 7.89% and 0.254 ms per batch; with CPU mask construction, host index/mask work totals 6.462 s.
ranked_evidence_for_next_change.next_experiment: Measure reuse or more direct construction of unchanged legal-move indices and masks without changing legal policy semantics.

ranked_evidence_for_next_change.evidence: CUDA-event model execution totals 6.450 s (0.331 ms per batch), while model-call host spans total 6.607 s; this is meaningful but far below CPU encoding.
ranked_evidence_for_next_change.next_experiment: Only after encoding work, evaluate safe launch/static-shape techniques against identical outputs.

ranked_evidence_for_next_change.evidence: Python result extraction is 1.788 s; H2D and D2H CUDA-event transfers total 1.790 s; explicit synchronization wait is only 0.069 s.
ranked_evidence_for_next_change.next_experiment: Do not prioritize synchronization or transfer changes before CPU encoding; measure any extraction change separately.

conclusion: The shared path is host-construction bound, specifically CPU encoding/stacking, not synchronization bound or GPU-compute saturated. This conclusion follows from direct host spans and CUDA events; the 2.24% nvidia-smi utilization sample is corroboration only.
